name_en: Akaneko — sticky rice and wheat mochi dusted with sweet soybean flour for the mid-summer rite
summary_ja: 蒸したもち米と小麦粉をついた餅に砂糖ときな粉をまぶす「半夏生もち」。田植えを終えた感謝と豊作祈願で食べられ、皮ごと挽いた小麦粉で餅が褐色になり、猫の丸い背中に似ることから名がついたと伝わる。
summary_en: Steamed sticky rice pounded with wheat flour is dusted with sugar and soybean flour — also called hangesho mochi, for the rite marking the end of rice planting. The whole-ground wheat flour once left the mochi brownish, said to resemble a cat's round back and give the dish its name.
source_title: あかねこ 大阪府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kurumi mochi — mochi wrapped in a sweet green soybean paste, a Sakai confection
summary_ja: 枝豆や青大豆をすりつぶしたうぐいす色の餡で餅を「くるんで」つくる堺の銘菓。クルミは使わない。海外貿易で栄えた戦国期の堺で生まれ、茶人・千利休の街らしく茶菓子として親しまれてきたという。
summary_en: Mochi is wrapped, or 'kurunde,' in a pale green paste of ground edamame or green soybeans — a confection of Sakai despite the name suggesting walnuts, which it does not contain. Born in Sakai's trading heyday, it is said to have long served as a tea sweet in the hometown of tea master Sen no Rikyu.
source_title: くるみ餅 大阪府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Osaka decchi yokan — a lightly-sweetened kanten yokan made with thread agar
summary_ja: 北摂地域特産の糸寒天でこしあんを固める、砂糖控えめの羊羹。練り羊羹より煮詰めが甘く一人前に満たないことから丁稚に見立てた説と、丁稚が里帰りの土産にしたという説があり、冬限定でつくられてきた。
summary_en: Sweet red bean paste is set with thread agar from the Hokusetsu area into a lightly sugared yokan. One theory ties its name to an apprentice, or decchi, not fully 'boiled down' like proper neri-yokan; another says apprentices carried it home as a gift. It is said to be made only in winter.
source_title: 丁稚ようかん 大阪府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Renkon mochi — lotus root stuffed with red-and-white sticky rice and steamed
summary_ja: 門真特産の蓮根「門真蓮根」の穴に紅白のもち米を詰めて蒸す、祝いの日の一品。穴が開いていることから「将来を見通せる」縁起物とされ、輪切りにしてきな粉やあんこ、からし醤油などで食べるという。
summary_en: Red and white sticky rice is packed into the holes of Kadoma renkon, a local lotus root, and steamed — a dish for celebrations. The root's holes are said to make it a lucky charm for 'seeing what lies ahead,' and slices are eaten with soybean flour, sweet bean paste, or mustard soy sauce.
source_title: 蓮根餅 大阪府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Osaka sakura mochi — sweet bean paste wrapped in a Domyoji rice-flour mochi
summary_ja: つぶつぶとした道明寺粉の餅であんを包み、塩漬けの桜の葉で巻く春の菓子。道明寺粉は千年以上前に藤井寺市の道明寺で保存食としてつくられたのが始まりとされ、関東のクレープ状の桜餅とは製法が異なる。
summary_en: Sweet bean paste is wrapped in a coarse-grained mochi made from domyoji rice flour, then bound with a salted cherry leaf — a springtime confection. Domyoji flour is said to have first been made over a thousand years ago as a preserved food at Domyoji temple in Fujiidera, giving a texture unlike Kanto's crepe-style sakura mochi.
source_title: 桜餅 大阪府 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
